proof_skeleton_nl: Use periodicity to reduce an arbitrary real x to its fractional part t in [0,1). Let m = floor(n*t). The floor characterization places t in the interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), and on that interval the expression is bounded above by the discrete surrogate g_n(m). The finite bottleneck lemma shows g_n(m) <= H_n - 1 for all m, so f_n(x) <= H_n - 1 for every x. On the other hand, if t is in the top interval [1 - 1/n,1), then every floor(k*t) equals k - 1, so f_n(t) = H_n - 1. The strict part of the discrete bottleneck excludes all other intervals. Therefore the maximum is H_n - 1, achieved exactly when the fractional part of x lies in [1 - 1/n,1).

steps.derives: For an arbitrary real x, replace x by its fractional part t = x - floor(x); then t lies in [0,1) and f_n(x) = f_n(t).
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct application of integer-shift periodicity together with the standard decomposition x = floor(x) + (x - floor(x)).

steps.derives: If m = floor(n*t), then t lies in the half-open interval [m/n, (m+1)/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the floor-interval characterization stated in the lemma.

steps.derives: For that m, the reduced value f_n(t) is at most g_n(m).
steps.trivial_justification: The lemma directly gives the interval-wise upper bound.

steps.derives: Since g_n(m) <= H_n - 1 for every admissible m, it follows that f_n(x) <= H_n - 1 for every real x.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct substitution of the discrete bound into the interval bound, together with the reduction from A1.

steps.derives: Every real x whose fractional part lies in [1 - 1/n, 1) satisfies f_n(x) = H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply the explicit evaluation on the top interval to the fractional part of x, using periodicity from A1.

steps.derives: If the fractional part t of x satisfies t < 1 - 1/n, then m = floor(n*t) is at most n - 2, so the equality case in L5 does not occur and f_n(x) < H_n - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: This combines the interval description of floor(n*t) with the strict part of the discrete maximization lemma.

steps.derives: The global maximum of f_n is H_n - 1, and the maximizers are exactly the real numbers x whose fractional part lies in [1 - 1/n, 1), equivalently x in Z + [1 - 1/n, 1).
steps.trivial_justification: A4 gives the global upper bound, A5 gives attainment on the stated interval, and A6 rules out all other fractional parts.
